title: Low distant M5.5+ counts exceeded a same-year shift reference after M7.5+ earthquakes in 2001-2024
abstract: We tested low distant earthquake counts in a fixed global ComCat snapshot. We used 125 M7.5+ centers in 2001-2024 and counted M5.5+ neighbors above 500 km in the next five days. Fifteen centers (12.0%) had counts below their same-year control tenth percentile. The common yearly shift reference had a mean of 6.25%, a central 95% range of 2.4-11.2%, and a one-sided Monte Carlo p-value of 0.0153. Integer count ties made the expected strict low fraction smaller than 10%. A delayed five-day window gave p=0.0676. No strict low windows occurred among 26 M8+ centers. An independent count audit passed. Exact control cutoffs left the primary observed count unchanged. The result supports a limited catalog association under a time-shift assumption. It does not show physical suppression, stress release or a hazard change. Revised records, mixed magnitudes, shared events, control timing and short-term detection loss limit inference.

display.caption: Observed low-window fractions and central 95% time-shift ranges. These ranges are null-model ranges, not effect confidence intervals. Strict and inclusive cutoffs have different reference rates because counts are integers.
